title: Small complete cotorsion pairs of flat sheaf complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A)$ its unbounded cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Write $\mathcal W$ for the acyclic complexes [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] and $\mathcal D$ for the complexes with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] which are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For complexes $P,T$, put $\operatorname{Hom}^{r}(P,T)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P^n,T^{n+r})$ with differential $h\mapsto d_T h-(-1)^r h d_P$; this is a complex of abelian groups, using global module morphisms, not internal sheaf Hom. In either abelian category, $\operatorname{Ext}^1(U,V)=0$ means that every short exact sequence $0\to V\to E\to U\to0$ splits. A module $T$ is cotorsion when $\operatorname{Ext}^1(F,T)=0$ for every flat module $F$.

Let $\mathcal E$ consist of complexes $T$ whose terms are cotorsion and for which $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(P,T)$ is acyclic for every $P\in\mathcal D\cap\mathcal W$. Let $\mathcal E_0$ consist of complexes $T$ whose terms are cotorsion and for which $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(P,T)$ is acyclic for every $P\in\mathcal D$. Then $\mathcal E_0=\mathcal E\cap\mathcal W$, and $(\mathcal D,\mathcal E_0)$ and $(\mathcal D\cap\mathcal W,\mathcal E)$ are complete hereditary small cotorsion pairs in $\mathcal B$.

Here a cotorsion pair $(\mathcal L,\mathcal T)$ means $\mathcal L={}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal T=\mathcal L^{\perp_1}$, with orthogonality defined by vanishing of $\operatorname{Ext}^1$. Complete means that every $X$ occurs in short exact sequences $0\to T\to L\to X\to0$ and $0\to X\to T'\to L'\to0$ with $L,L'\in\mathcal L$ and $T,T'\in\mathcal T$. Hereditary means that the left class is closed under kernels of epimorphisms between its objects and the right class under cokernels of monomorphisms between its objects. Small means that there is a set $I$ of monomorphisms with cokernels in $\mathcal L$ such that the maps with the right lifting property against $I$ are exactly the epimorphisms with kernel in $\mathcal T$. The right lifting property means that every commutative square with left map in $I$ admits a diagonal making its two triangles commute. No enough-projectives, enough-points, or sectionwise-flatness hypothesis is imposed.
